questions.question: Who among the following organised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as a part of his constructive programme for the removal of untouchability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

__
 
• **Harijan Sevak Sangh was organized by Mahatma Gandhi in 1932** as a part of his **constructive program for the removal of untouchability.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Its parent organization was the **All India Anti Untouchability League founded by Mahatma Gandhi earlier on 30 September 1932. **
 
• This was later renamed **Harijan Sevak Sangh. **
 
• Its first president was **Ghanshyam Das Birla and the secretary was Amritlal Takkar.**
 
• It still exists as a non – governmental organization working for the welfare of **Harijan or Dalit people and upliftment of the Depressed Class of India.**

questions.question: In which of the following cities was the Veda Samaj established in 1864?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Madras(Chennai).__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Veda Samaj was established by Keshab Chandra Sen and K. Sridharalu Naidu.**
 
• **Established in Madras (Chennai) in 1864.**
 
• The Veda Samaj was inspired by the **Brahmo Samaj.**
 
• It worked to abolish caste distinctions and promote widow remarriage and women's education.
 
• Its members believed in one God. 
 
• They condemned the superstitions and rituals of orthodox Hinduism.
 
• An important ideology of the members of **Veda Samaj** was regarding marriage and the funeral rituals as matters of routine, destitute of all religious significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• It was started at Calcutta on **20 August in 1828** by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**
 
• It was a** monotheistic sect of Hinduism.**
 
• **Brahmo samaj **had no faith in any scripture as an authority.
 
• It rejects incarnation.
 
• It was against caste restrictions and propounded a mix of west-east religious qualities.
 
• It denounced polytheism and idol worship opposed idolatry.
 
• It denied the need for a priestly class for interpreting religious texts.
 
• Brahmo Samaj spread the religious treasure and teachings of Vedas but never claimed that Vedas are infallible.

questions.question: Who founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sir William Jones**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Asiatic Society of Bengal was founded on Jan 15, 1784**, by **Sir William Jones**, an Orientalist, to encourage Oriental studies.
 
• An outstanding scholar from the University of Oxford, arrived in Calcutta (now Kolkata) in 1783, as a **supreme court judge**. The society was founded after his arrival.
 
• The Asiatic Society had the** support of Warren Hastings**, the Governor-General (1772–85) of Bengal.
 
• The society owns an** art collection** which includes paintings by Peter Paul Rubens and Joshua Reynolds.
 
• **Indians were first admitted as members of the Asiatic Society in 1829.**
 
• The society’s library contains some 100,000 general volumes, and more than 27,000 books o Sanskrit, manuscripts, prints, coins, and engravings.
 
• The **Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal** is published regularly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• West Bengal is a state in **eastern India**, between the Himalayas and the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Its capital, Kolkata (formerly Calcutta), retains **architectural and cultural remnants **of its past as an East India Company trading post and capital of the British Raj.
 
• Trinamool leader **Mamata Banerjee** is **West Bengal's incumbent chief minister**, the first woman to hold the office.
 
• **Shri C V Anand ** assumed charge of the office of the **Governor of West Bengal** on 18th July 2022.

questions.question: In which year did Ambedkar start a temple entry movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1927**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• T emple Entry Movement was founded by Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar in **1927**.
 
• It was a movement to allow lower caste people to enter temples.
 
• ​Untouchables were treated as inferior human beings, they were not allowed entry inside the temples, they could not bathe in ponds used by upper-caste people and they could not use the wells used by upper-caste people.
 
• A temple entry movement was started by Dr B.R. Ambedkar in 1927.
 
• This temple entry movement saw the participation of people from the Mahar Caste.
 
• Between 1927 and 1935, Dr B.R. Ambedkar led three temple entry movements.
 
• The objective of the temple entry movement led by Dr B.R. Ambedkar was to expose the caste prejudices that existed within Indian society.
 
• Dr B.R. Ambedkar was born into a Mahar family.
 
• Ambedkar had faced caste discrimination right from his childhood.
 
• Ambedkar was not allowed to drink water from the taps that were used by upper-caste children.
 
• After f inishing his higher education in the US, Ambedkar returned to India in 1919 and extensively wrote about caste-based discrimination in Indian society.

questions.concept: Religious and Philosophical Ideas, Buddhism
questions.question: Who among the following gave most of his preaching at 'Gridhrakuta'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gautama Buddha**__.

__
 
• **Gautama Buddha** gave most of his preaching at '**Gridhrakuta**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

**​** **Gautama Buddha**, also known as Siddhartha Gautama, was an Indian prince who renounced his privileged life to seek spiritual enlightenment.

__
 
• After years of wandering and meditation, he attained enlightenment under a bodhi tree in Bodh Gaya, India.
 
• Following his enlightenment, Buddha began teaching his philosophy and path to enlightenment, known as Buddhism, to others.
 
• He traveled throughout northern India and Nepal, preaching and teaching in various places.
 
• One of the most significant places where Buddha gave his sermons was **Gridhrakuta**, or **Vulture's Peak**.
 
 
• It is said that Buddha spent many rainy seasons at Gridhrakuta, where he gave several important sermons, including the Lotus Sutra and the Heart Sutra.
 
 
 
• **Gridhrakuta **is located in **Rajgir, Bihar, **India, and is considered to be one of the most important Buddhist pilgrimage sites.
 
• The mountain is shaped like a vulture, hence its name, and is believed to be the site where Buddha preached his most important teachings.

In summary, **Gautama Buddha gave most of his preaching at Gridhrakuta, a mountain in Rajgir, Bihar, India, where he delivered many important sermons, including the Lotus Sutra and the Heart Sutra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vardhamana Mahavira**

 
 
• 24th Tirthankara of Jainism
 
• Born - 540 B.C.(Kundagrama near Vaishali).
 
• Clan - Jnatrika clan
 
• First sermon - Pava.
 
• Mahavira’s symbol - lion.
 
• Death- At the age of 72 in 468 B.C. at the Pavapuri in Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Guru Nanak Dev**
 
 
• **​**Born: 15 April 1469, Nankana Sahib
 
• Died: 22 September 1539, Kartarpur
 
• He was the founder of Sikhism.
 
• He is also the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Paramhansa**
 
 
• Born: 18 February 1836, Kamarpukur
 
• Died: 16 August 1886, Cossipore
 
• He was an Indian Hindu religious leader in the 19th century.
 
• He is also the teacher of Swami Vivekananda.

questions.question: In which year was the All India Kisan Sabha founded in Lucknow with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as the president?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1936.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__​**

__
 
• The All India Kisan Sabha was formed in 1936 at Lucknow.
 
• All India Kisan Sabha is also known as ‘Akhil Bhartiya Kisan Sabha.’
 
• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was the President of the Sabha.
 
• The secretary of All India Kisan Sabha was NG Ranga.
 
• The motives of the All India Kisan Sabha were:
 
 
• To abolish the Zamindari system,
 
• To reduce land revenue,
 
• To institutionalize credit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Kisan Sabha movement was started in Bihar under the leadership of Sahajanand Saraswati.
 
• It was formed in 1929 by the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in order to mobilize peasants and vocalize their grievances against the zamindari attacks on their occupancy rights and thus sparking the farmers' movements in India.
 
• Gradually the peasant movement intensified and spread across the rest of India.
 
• The formation of the Congress Socialist Party (CSP) in 1934 helped the Communists to work together with the INC, however temporarily, then in April 1935, noted peasant leaders N. G. Ranga and E. M. S. Namboodiripad, then secretary and joint secretary respectively of South Indian Federation of Peasants and Agricultural Labour suggested the formation of an all-India farmers body.
 
• Soon all these radical developments culminated in the formation of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress on 11 April 1936 with **Swami Sahajanand** Saraswati elected as its first President.
 
• It involved people such as Ranga, Namboodiripad, Karyanand Sharma, Yamuna Karjee, Yadunandan (Jadunandan) Sharma, Rahul Sankrityayan, P. Sundarayya, Ram Manohar Lohia, Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev and Bankim Mukherjee.
 
• The Kisan Manifesto released in August 1936, demanded the abolition of the zamindari system and cancellation of rural debts, and in October 1937, it adopted the red flag as its banner.
 
• Soon, its leaders became increasingly** distant from Congress **and repeatedly came into confrontation with Congress governments, in Bihar and United Province.

questions.question: Which of the following organizations was established earlier than the other three organizations during the British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmo Samaj.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **The Brahmo Samaj** was formed in **1828.**

 
 
• It prohibited all forms of idolatry and sacrifice, believed in the Upanishads and forbade its members from criticising other religious practices.
 
 
 
• **The Prarthana Samaj **was founded in **1867 in Bombay by Dr Atmaram Pandurang.**
 
 
• It was an off-shoot of Brahmo Samaj.
 
• It was a reform movement within Hinduism and Justice M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar joined it in **1870 **and infused new strength to it.
 
 
 
• **Paramahansa Mandali **was a secret socio-religious group,** established in 1849,** in Bombay and is closely related to Manav Dharma Sabha.
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj **(Truth-seekers' Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on** 24 September 1873.**
 
• **Hence Brahmo Samaj was established earlier than the other three organizations.**

questions.question: When was the Indian Reform Association formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1870**__.

__
 
• **The Indian Reform Association was formed on 29 October 1870 with Keshub Chunder Sen as president**__.

 __
 
• It represented the secular side of the Brahmo Samaj and included many who did not belong to the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The objective was to put into practice some of the ideas Sen was exposed to during his English visit**.
 
• The work of the Association was divided into five departments– **cheap literature, female improvement, education, temperance, and charity. **
 
• The female normal school was started in February 1871 under the auspices of the female improvement section for adult ladies who wanted to be taught or to learn how to teach. Subsequently, a girls’ school was attached wherein the adult students of the normal school could learn and practice the art of teaching. A carefully devised syllabus laid stress on womanly virtues and accomplishments.
 
• **The third section dealing with education undertook to educate the labouring classes** and to instruct the middle classes in industrial arts.
 
• The Working Men’s Institution and the Industrial School were opened on 28 November 1870.

questions.question: Identify the correctly matched pair of the founder and the social/socio-religious organisation founded.

options.text: Raja Ram Mohan Ray – Arya Samaj

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda – Ramakrishna Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission** is an **Indian socio-religious organization** founded by **Swami Vivekanand on 1 May 1897**. 
 
• It was established in order to propagate the **ideals of Ramakrishna Paramahasa**. 
 
• It conducts research in the field of **health care, elementary and higher education, tribal welfare, and culture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:-**

 
 
• It is the society of **Nobles vigorous reform movement of modern Hinduism**, founded in **1875 by Dayananda Sarasvati.**
 
• **Aim:- ** To reestablish the Vedas, the earliest Hindu scriptures, as revealed truth. 
 
• The Arya Samaj opposes worship of murtis (images), animal sacrifice, shraddha (rituals on behalf of ancestors), basing caste upon birth rather than upon merit, untouchability, child marriage, pilgrimages, priestly craft, and temple offerings. 
 
• It has worked to further **female education and inter caste marriage**, has built missions, orphanages, and homes for widows, has established a network of schools and colleges; and has undertaken famine relief and medical work. 
 
• From its beginning, it was an important factor in the **growth of Indian nationalism**. 
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:-**
 
 
• It is an atheistic** movement within Hinduism**, founded in **Kolkata in 1828 by Ram Mohan Roy**. 
 
• It does not accept the authority of the Vedas, has no faith in avatars (incarnations), and does not insist on belief in karma (causal effects of past deeds) or samsara (the process of death and rebirth).
 
• It discards Hindu rituals and denounces **polytheism, image worship, and the caste system**.
